newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end off amid foreign disinterest.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end off amid foreign disinterest.

text.p: Mexican stock traders had their annual dose of Christmas cheer Monday but it did little to offset the market's fourth straight slump as mariachi singers strolled onto the floor at the closing bell for a holiday celebration.
"No one wanted to trade. Interest in Mexico is going from bad to worse. We spent the day just waiting for the bell and the waiters to appear," said a floor trader.
The blue-chip IPC index closed off 30.12 points, or 0.94 percent, at 3,175.09. Volume was a lifeless 33.6 million shares.

While traders were celebrating, analysts expressed concern over the bourse's continuing slide, which they put down to lack of interest among foreign investors and forecast hikes in primary interest rates on Tuesday.

"The bourse was again hit by a lack of foreign investors, and was further hurt by forecasts that Cetes hikes would be greater than previously expected," said Roberto Galvan, an anlyst at the Bursametrica consultancy.
Money market dealers estimated that bellwether 28-day Cetes (Treasury bill) rates could gain one-half to one percentage point at Tuesday's primary auction of government securities.
Another trader said the market was stifled by lingering political concerns in the wake of the weekend's changeover in chairmanship of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party.
"We wanted to see how they took the changes in leadership, people are more concerned over that than anything else," a floor trader said.
Traders said the listless market was almost oblivious to the announcement that industrial output in October gained 15.5 percent in year-ago terms.
On the broad market, 96 stocks were traded, with gainers trouncing losers 58 to 17.
A notable gainer, traders said, was food company Grupo Corvi, up 12 centavos (2 cents) to 5.80 pesos (74 cents), following its upgrading to long-term buy from hold by the Interacciones brokerage.

Debt-stricken holding company Sidek headed the losers, followed by financial stocks GFNorte and Abacogf which traders said were overshadowed by the forthcoming introduction of international accountancy criteria.

Sidek fell 6 centavos (1 cent) to 63 centavos (8 cents), while GFNorte and Abacogf ended off 60 centavos (8 cents) and 13 centavos (2 cents), respectively, at 7.08 (90 cents) and 2.47 pesos (31 cents).
The new criteria would increase estimates of burgeoning past-due loans and force banks to create more reserves, traders added.
